## 2026-07-08 Field Frame P0 Route-Bound Post-Resolution Still-Blocked Readiness Binding

Bound the post-resolution execution route still-blocked review into the
route-bound readiness blocker map as an explicit source report and ready input.
This keeps the positive-chain path fail-closed after authorization intake result
resolution: the post-resolution route is reviewed and source-index bound, but no
post-resolution unblock receipt or route-bound execution receipt is present or
accepted. No real route identity readback receipt, route selection record,
route-bound authorization evidence, rejection receipt, deployment, target visual
capture, touch proof, target IME matrix, status publication, product claim, or
public release was opened.

Changed source-side guards:

- `field-frame-p0-route-bound-readiness-blocker-map` now explicitly requires
  `post_resolution_execution_route_still_blocked` in `source_reports`,
  `post_resolution_execution_route_still_blocked_locked` in `ready_inputs`, and
  both `post_resolution_unblock_receipt_absent` plus
  `route_bound_execution_receipt_absent` in blockers.
- The readiness map now reports 22 gates, 10 source reports, 10 ready inputs,
  12 blockers, 10 resolved reports, 10 source report bindings, and
  `post_resolution_execution_route_still_blocked_source_count=1`.
- The readiness map report now emits
  `post_resolution_execution_route_unblocked_count=0`,
  `post_resolution_unblock_receipt_present_count=0`, and
  `route_bound_execution_receipt_present_count=0`.
- `resident-no-device-guard-suite-smoke.sh` now asserts those readiness fields
  and requires the resolved report id
  `post_resolution_execution_route_still_blocked` before the suite can pass.

Closed the remaining epoch long-tail resident-suite weak `latest` consumer
slice in `resident-no-device-guard-suite-smoke.sh`. The last sixteen
resident-suite epoch reports now resolve through `suite_report_or_latest_report`;
in zero-fallback suite context they must be bound by suite/log/seed/source
indexes, and their validation sites re-check the resolved path through

resident suite ...` fallback paths. The only remaining

## 2026-07-08 Field Frame P0 Post-Suite Index-Bound Consumer Closure

Closed the next post-suite consumer surface where the no-device suite could
still accept a resolved post-refusal report after the suite without proving that
the path came from the suite/log/seed indexes. The no-device suite script now
has suite-aware report validation helpers: `normalize_target_report_path`,
`report_index_contains_report`, and `require_suite_resolved_report`. Under
`RESIDENT_REQUIRE_NO_GLOBAL_REPORT_FALLBACKS=true`, the post-refusal after-suite
consumer checks now require every resolved report to exist under `target/` and
to be bound by `suite-report-index.txt`, `suite-child-report-index.txt`,
`suite-seed-report-index.txt`, or `suite-source-report-index.txt`; otherwise
the suite fails closed instead of treating a weak post-suite "latest" result as
valid.

chain that still had source-report discovery fallback risk across quorum,
delegation, countersignature, review-attestation, and issuer-revocation guards.
Thirteen tail guards now use the repo-local suite index helper for
suite/source/seed-report/seed-source lookup, fail closed with explicit
latest-fallback refusal under suite context when indexed evidence is missing,

not define that helper themselves.

## 2026-07-07 Field Frame P0 Native Focus Source Index Fetch Cache Closure

Closed the interrupted native focus source-index round and the release-blocking
blocker it exposed. The native text-input compositor/OSK focus-restore spike
guard now consumes suite/source/seed-report/seed-source index handoffs for the
input-method text commit probe path, validates seed index SHA256 handoffs, and
fails closed in suite context instead of falling back to latest target discovery.

The follow-up full suite exposed a separate robustness gap in the native
input-method activation source patch spike guard: a transient `curl` failure
could leave the Phoc orig tarball absent, after which the script proceeded to
`tar` and failed late. The source fetch helper now:

- verifies existing source artifacts against fixed SHA256 values before reuse;
- reuses repo-local cached source artifacts from prior target runs when they
  match the expected SHA256;
- retries downloads with `--retry`, bounded connect/max time, and a secondary
  Ubuntu mirror;
- rejects unverified or partial source artifacts before extraction.

## 2026-07-07 Field Frame P0 UI Route Review Cross Binding Source Index Consumption Closure

Closed a manifest-integrity downstream consumer fallback gap in the UI progress
route review cross-binding guard. The guard already supported explicit
path+SHA256 input reports, but its no-explicit-env path only treated
`RESIDENT_SUITE_REPORT_INDEX` as suite context. A suite run using only
`RESIDENT_SUITE_SOURCE_REPORT_INDEX`, `RESIDENT_SUITE_SEED_REPORT_INDEX`, or
`RESIDENT_SUITE_SEED_SOURCE_REPORT_INDEX` could therefore still reach latest
target discovery. The resolver now consumes suite/source/seed-report/seed-source
indexes, validates seed index SHA256 handoffs, and refuses latest fallback
whenever any suite index context is active.

Code/source changes:

- Added suite-indexed report lookup for the six cross-binding inputs: UI
  progress plan audit, live current-risk rollup, current-risk future-plan
  cross-binding, live real-receipt intake target-route materialization, live
  current-risk to real-receipt intake evidence boundary, and the route review
  cross-binding report.
- Required `RESIDENT_SUITE_SEED_REPORT_INDEX_SHA256` and
  `RESIDENT_SUITE_SEED_SOURCE_REPORT_INDEX_SHA256` before consuming seed index
  handoffs, and rejected bad seed-source SHA values.
- Added an all-suite-index-context fallback guard so source-only and seed-source
  suite contexts fail closed instead of falling through to target/latest report
  discovery.
- Marked suite-indexed cross-binding inputs as six source-bound SHA-checked
  inputs so the existing pass semantics remain strict and explicit handoff
  semantics are preserved.

suite-report-index-only source handoff behavior. The patched Phoc deployment
authorization, target-IME deployment route selection, native activation commit
proof closure, and Phoc patched deployment execution authorization hold guards
now resolve upstream evidence from suite/source/seed-report/seed-source indexes
with seed index SHA256 validation. In suite context, missing indexed upstream
evidence fails closed and refuses target/latest fallback. Explicit path+SHA
handoff remains supported.

Code/source changes:

- Expanded the four Phoc/deployment tail source-bound hold guards to the same
  four indexed handoff sources used by the rest of the no-device suite tail.
- Counted suite/source/seed-index hits as source-bound evidence in each hold
  guard while preserving explicit path+SHA semantics.
- Required SHA256 validation for seed report and seed source report indexes.
- Disabled target/latest fallback whenever any suite context is active.
- Fixed bad explicit SHA handling so hold guards emit blocked JSON instead of
  exiting early under `set -e`.
- Updated the target-IME deployment route selection source-bound runner's
  implicit latest fallback redteam to run against an intentionally empty suite
  source index, preserving fail-closed coverage after indexed handoff support.
- Restored executable mode on the patched Phoc deployment authorization hold
  guard so the no-device suite can invoke it directly.

## 2026-05-25 Android-Native Lineage-Hosted Control Plane Complete

After the known-good LineageOS fogos rescue baseline was booted, the rebuild
line pivoted away from reflashing the failed Mobian/super/vbmeta artifact
family. The safe route is now Lineage-hosted Android-native control-plane
delivery.

The local rebuild chain first extracted the official LineageOS dynamic
partition map and images, rebuilt a known-good slot-b `super` locally, extracted
known-good `vbmeta`/`vbmeta_system`, and built a rollback bundle before any new
target write. It then built a minimal Trillionnium overlay packet, staged it
under `/data/local/tmp/trillionnium`, extracted it on target, and verified both
archive SHA256 and embedded packet `SHA256SUMS` on the phone. No flash or reboot
occurred in this chain.

Runtime probing found the expected blocker for the old payload: the staged
`trillionniumd` and `trillionnium-shell` Mobian binaries are GNU/Linux glibc
payloads using `/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1`, while the rescued Lineage target
has no `su` and no glibc loader. Those payloads were kept inert.

## 2026-05-24 Target Hardware Both-Slots Fallthrough, Known-Good Intake Blocked

Under Alex's blanket/highest authorization, the target-hardware flash line crossed
the real destructive Fastboot execution boundary and then stopped at a recovery
hard blocker.

The final destructive executor flashed `boot_a`, `boot_b`, `vendor_boot_a`,
`vendor_boot_b`, `dtbo_a`, `dtbo_b`, `vbmeta_a`, and `vbmeta_b`, then failed
closed at `vbmeta_system_a` preflash validation. Recovery continuation generated
a rollback28/location0 `vbmeta_system.img`, flashed `vbmeta_system_a`,
`vbmeta_system_b`, and `super`, then rebooted. Post-reboot transport recovery
restored Fastboot/USB visibility only; ADB never returned.

Both boot slots were then tried through guarded recovery:

- `set_active b` succeeded, rebooted, and fell through to Fastboot.
- diagnosis selected slot-a fallback.
- `set_active a` succeeded, rebooted, and also fell through to Fastboot.

Current bootloader state from the final recovery summary: Fastboot visible,
USB visible, ADB absent, product `fogos`, `current-slot` empty, running
bootloader slot `_a/_a`, slot-successful a/b `no`, slot-unbootable a/b `yes`,

## 2026-05-21 Droidian/Halium Base Pivot

After touch UI response was confirmed, the phone bring-up strategy moved away
from continued one-off vendor_boot/initramfs micro-probes. The next technical
foundation is a Droidian/Halium-compatible Android hardware-adaptation base:
Motorola/FOGOS Android base as donor, Android HAL sidecar through
Halium/libhybris-style interfaces, Debian/Mobian as the primary userspace, Phosh
as shell, and `trillionniumd`/Hepta as the capability layer.

This is not a direct LineageOS product fork. LineageOS/AOSP/CAF/stock Motorola
artifacts are donor inputs for kernel, vendor BSP, proprietary blobs, Android
services, and HAL contracts. Sailfish HADK is used as a process reference for
Android-base validation and hardware-adaptation discipline, not as a UI/package
stack. Ubuntu Touch remains a Halium reference, not the product target.

The architecture decision is recorded in
`docs/architecture/2026-05-21-droidian-halium-base-pivot.md`.

Immediate next gates:

- `android-base-donor-inventory-smoke`
- `halium-droidian-kernel-config-gap-smoke`
- `android-hal-sidecar-rootfs-plan-smoke`
- `halium-sidecar-first-boot-smoke`
- `hardware-subsystem-matrix-smoke`
- `release-readiness-review`

The existing vendor_boot capsule and USB status channel remain valuable as
bring-up, recovery, and observability surfaces. They are no longer the intended
place to solve every hardware subsystem one by one.

  binder/binderfs proof, LXC namespace/cgroup proof, module inventory, and

  plan: Debian/Mobian + Phosh remains the primary userspace; Android is a HAL
  and vendor-service sidecar under `trillionnium-android-hal-sidecar`, not the
  product UI.
- `halium-sidecar-first-boot-smoke` locks the first-boot contract only. It does
  not start a sidecar or execute target hardware. The future target boot must
  prove harmless `getprop` and binder service discovery through USB status.
- `hardware-subsystem-matrix-smoke` records the current subsystem state:

## 2026-05-21 Lineage Root Container Dogfood Fast Lane

After Alex asked whether LineageOS plus a root chroot/container would be much
faster than the Droidian/Halium path, the answer was recorded as a separate
fast dogfood lane: yes for interactive control-plane iteration, no as a
replacement for the final OS architecture.

The new `lineage-root-container-dogfood-smoke` gate locks this distinction. It
keeps LineageOS/Android as the hardware owner and treats the existing arm64
Mobian/Trillionnium rootfs as a guest payload for a future root
chroot/container. This avoids first solving every kernel, binderfs/LXC, sidecar,
and subsystem receipt before dogfooding Trillionnium services. It does not make
the product a LineageOS fork, does not claim a full Trillionnium OS phone boot,
and does not change the release verdict.

## 2026-05-21 Lineage Root Container Live Dogfood Runtime

Alex then authorized the destructive restore with
`授权恢复 Lineage Android ADB 快线`. The restore receipt gate executed the
previously locked template against true `ZY32JLVHGN` bootloader fastboot,
restored Lineage 23.2 / Android ADB, and reached `sys.boot_completed=1`.
That crossed the destructive restore boundary, but it did not execute a release
push.

After Lineage ADB returned, the first root-container preflight proved the ADB
path but blocked on missing root. A non-persistent Magisk tempboot was then
prepared from the current Lineage boot image and run with `fastboot boot`,
not `fastboot flash`. Magisk 30.6 became current, Shell superuser was granted,
and `/debug_ramdisk/su -c id` returned `uid=0(root)` in `u:r:magisk:s0`.

With root available, the authorized root-container preflight passed: the arm64
Trillionnium/Mobian rootfs was pushed under `/data/local/tmp`, mounted through
root, and `trillionniumd --print-manifest` executed inside the chroot. The
runtime endpoint gate then started a localhost service inside the Lineage-hosted
root-container path. The interactive control-plane gate forwarded it to the host
through ADB at `http://127.0.0.1:18080/status.json` and
`http://127.0.0.1:18080/manifest.json`.

Current development position is **dogfood control-plane RC**, not full
Trillionnium OS on-device release.

Promoted evidence now distinguishes three layers:

- Mobian/Phosh Trillionnium OS artifacts are ready to build locally
  (`ready_for_build=true`) and have rootfs, disk-layout, emulator, UEFI/initrd,
  recovery-handoff, and package/install evidence.
- The physical ZY32JLVHGN device evidence is FOGOS/Lineage Android 16 with the
  `ai.trillionnium.bridge` dogfood package installed and smoke-tested.
- The phone is not booted into a full Trillionnium OS image:
  `ready_for_flash=false`, `ready_for_install=false`,
  `on_device_trillionnium_os_ready=false`, and `ready_for_release_push=false`.

`packaging/mobian/scripts/on-device-trillionnium-os-smoke.sh` is the boundary
gate that locks this interpretation. It runs read-only ADB identity/package
checks and passes only by proving the current hardware state is
FOGOS/Lineage-hosted Bridge dogfood, not a full Trillionnium OS phone boot.
Any claim that the phone has Trillionnium OS installed still needs a separate
target-hardware Trillionnium OS install/flash/post-boot identity proof.

`packaging/mobian/scripts/target-trillionnium-os-readiness-smoke.sh` now locks
the next development frontier as a static readiness matrix. It separates the
currently promoted `amd64` Mobian/Phosh UEFI+initrd emulator boot and local
recovery handoff from the `arm64` FOGOS/Lineage target artifacts and from the
live Bridge dogfood phone. The result is explicit: target-hardware Trillionnium
OS artifact produced = false, target-hardware install executed = false,
target-hardware post-boot identity proof promoted = false, and release-push
ready = false.

`packaging/mobian/scripts/package-install-smoke.sh` now has a binary
architecture guard before `.deb` production, and
`packaging/mobian/scripts/arm64-trillionnium-package-preflight-smoke.sh`
records the current arm64 package frontier. On this host the existing debug
binaries started as `amd64`; real arm64 Trillionnium `.deb`/rootfs artifacts
remain blocked, but the package smoke can no longer silently relabel host
`amd64` binaries as arm64 packages.

`package-install-smoke.sh` is now target-aware for the next arm64 run:
`ARCH=arm64` defaults to `RUST_TARGET=aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, passes
`--target` to cargo, and reads binaries from
`target/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/debug`. The
`arm64-trillionnium-cross-build-path-smoke.sh` gate proves that path is wired
without running cargo/rustup/apt/dpkg-deb or producing arm64 binaries. The
current blocker has moved from package script plumbing to the actual
non-host-mutating aarch64 Rust/linker/sysroot path.

`packaging/mobian/scripts/arm64-private-toolchain-plan-smoke.sh` records that
next boundary without crossing it. It declares target-local `RUSTUP_HOME`,

`target/mobian-arm64-private-toolchain`, confirms local apt metadata has the
seed cross-package candidates, and writes command templates for a later private
fetch/build gate. It does not execute network downloads, `rustup`, `apt-get
download`, `apt install`, `dpkg-deb`, cargo build, package build, or any device
action.

## 2026-05-11

Started the OS implementation as a separate `trillionnium-os/` Rust workspace.

The current scope is deliberately narrow:

- define stable OS-facing types around the canonical Hepta runtime,
- add the OS policy/audit/tool-adapter validation loop,
- expose the first D-Bus `Ping` surface,
- keep mobile/desktop divergence out of the core,
- avoid building a second competing runtime inside Trillionnium OS.

The Dropbox Hepta snapshot is treated as the canonical runtime source and is
not edited by this Trillionnium OS pass.

M1 backend slice now exists:

- `trillionnium-task-registry` stores task views and approval requests in memory, with
  SQLite snapshot load/save handled by `trillionnium-audit-sqlite`.
- `org.trillionnium.Agent1` exposes JSON-string D-Bus methods for task creation,
  task listing, cancellation, approval request/approve/deny, approval listing,
  and audit timeline query.
- `org.trillionnium.Agent1` emits JSON-string `TaskCreated`, `TaskUpdated`,
  `ApprovalRequested`, `ApprovalDecided`, and `AuditEventAppended` signals.
- `trillionniumd --once smoke` exercises a real task + medium-risk approval + exact
  one-call grant path and writes SQLite audit rows plus task/approval snapshots.
- D-Bus smoke verified `CreateTask`, `ListTasks`, `RequestApproval`, `Approve`,
  `CancelTask`, `AuditTimeline`, signal emission, and restore after daemon
  restart.

M2 OS tool-adapter slice now exists:

- `trillionnium-os-types` now has persisted `ToolRun` state (`requested`,
  `waiting_for_approval`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, and
  `approval_granted_awaiting_retry`) with output/error/timestamps and stable
  JSON serialization tests.
- `trillionnium-tool-runtime` is a Trillionnium OS adapter/shim crate, not the canonical
  Hepta runtime. It exposes built-in manifests for low-risk `system.status` and
  safe medium-risk `demo.approval_echo`; those manifests are marked with
  `ToolExecutorKind::LocalShim`, only temporary local shim built-ins execute,
  and there is still no arbitrary shell execution path. It also exposes
  `runtime_adapter_probe()` so Command Center can show that LocalShim is ready
  while the native Hepta adapter is deliberately blocked until a stable direct
  invoke or supervised-sidecar contract exists. `runtime_adapter_contract()`
  exposes the non-executing draft native direct-invoke / sidecar boundary.
  `native_hepta_runtime_adapter_probe()` is feature-gated by
  `native-hepta-runtime-adapter`: default builds report disabled, while feature
  builds construct Hepta `RuntimeKernel`, map public descriptors into
  Trillionnium `ToolManifest`s, validate them, and prove `execute_tool` remains
  blocked so D-Bus/default execution stays on LocalShim. `status --json`, text
  status, and both GTK UI paths now carry the same display-only native-adapter
  snapshot in the runtime section. `hepta_catalog_probe()`
  is feature-gated by `hepta-catalog-probe` to read Hepta
  `RuntimeKernel::tool_descriptors()` as descriptor-only summaries.
  `hepta_schema_crosswalk_report()` shares the `hepta-catalog-probe` gate and
  compiles every Hepta descriptor input/output schema into a Trillionnium
  manifest-shaped validation report with registration explicitly disabled.
  `hepta_sidecar_mock_report()` validates the supervised sidecar request/response
  envelope, request/correlation id echo, blocked invoke path, and event-cursor
  progression without opening a socket or invoking Hepta. `runtime sidecar-noop`
  then spawns a real no-op child process, connects over a temporary Unix socket,
  verifies health/query-events, confirms `invoke_tool` is blocked, and shuts the
  child down cleanly. `runtime sidecar-supervise` repeats the same no-op lifecycle
  on the canonical `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/trillionnium-os/hepta-runtime.sock` path with
  separate client connections and refuses to take over an active socket. The dogfood
  packaging now renders a disabled-by-default `trillionnium-hepta-sidecar-noop.service`
  template for the same blocked sidecar child. `runtime sidecar-status` inspects
  the packaged unit and canonical socket read-only, reports static/inactive as the
  safe default, and sends only `health`/`query_events` if a sidecar is already
  running. `runtime sidecar-events` then maps read-only `query_events` output from
  an already-running sidecar into cursor/limit-controlled audit-shaped preview rows,
  exportable as JSON/JSONL/Markdown/CSV, while keeping SQLite writes, D-Bus
  signals, registration, and `invoke_tool` disabled. `doctor`, `status`, and the
  GTK/libadwaita UI surface passive sidecar state; `status` and UI now also show
  sidecar event preview cursor/counts and audit-shaped preview rows, while the UI
  exposes command-hint buttons for current preview, next cursor, and JSONL export
  without requiring the sidecar to be enabled or started.
  `runtime sidecar-invoke-probe` is the first feature-gated real sidecar invoke
  gate: default builds report disabled, while `hepta-sidecar-invoke-probe` builds
  spawn an ephemeral child on a temporary socket, construct Hepta `RuntimeKernel`,
  list descriptors, validate `echo`, run one low-risk `echo` invocation through
  Hepta's public `run_demo_turn_in_session` path, query events, and shut down.
  The probe is child-local, echo-only, read-only-profiled, and keeps packaged
  sidecar state, D-Bus registration, Trillionnium audit writes, and default
  LocalShim execution unchanged. `hepta_ollama_toolcall_probe()` is a separate
  `hepta-ollama-toolcall-probe` local-only smoke that imports Ollama's
  OpenAI-compatible endpoint into Hepta, selects the local Gemma model, installs
  a deny-by-default provider policy, allowlists only `echo`, and verifies one
  real Hepta tool call without making Hepta the default Trillionnium executor.
- `trillionnium-audit-sqlite` now persists `tool_runs` alongside audit events, tasks,
  and approvals.
- `org.trillionnium.Agent1` exposes `ListTools`, `RunTool`, `RetryToolRun`, and
  `ListToolRuns` JSON-string methods. `RunTool(system.status)` executes
  immediately. Running `demo.approval_echo` creates a pending approval;
  `Approve` grants one-call permission and resumes the saved tool run to
  completion. `RetryToolRun` re-submits a persisted failed or
  approval-granted-awaiting-retry run through the same validation/policy/audit
  path while preserving the original tool-call id.
- Tool lifecycle audit rows are written for `tool_requested`,
  `policy_evaluated`, `approval_requested`, `approval_decided`, `tool_started`,
  and `tool_finished`/`tool_failed`.
- D-Bus signals now include `ToolRequested`, `PolicyEvaluated`, `ToolStarted`,
  `ToolFinished`, and `ToolFailed` in addition to the task/approval/audit
  signals from M1.

M3-pre Command Center slice now exists:

- `apps/trillionnium-command-center` is a workspace member. The default path remains a
  terminal/text-mode shell, and a first GTK/libadwaita UI shell now compiles
  behind the `ui` Cargo feature.
- The app has clean CLI/dashboard/D-Bus/local-state/render module boundaries so
  the GTK/libadwaita shell reuses the same dashboard model instead of forking
  daemon/task/approval/audit/tool/policy logic.
- `status` tries `org.trillionnium.Agent1` over the session D-Bus, summarizes daemon
  version/start time plus task, approval, tool-run, and audit timeline state,
  and falls back to local SQLite snapshots when the daemon/session bus is
  unavailable.
- `smoke` builds an offline demo task + pending approval + in-memory SQLite
  audit/tool-run timeline, validates all built-in tool manifests, and probes
  low, medium, high, and critical policy decisions.
- `ui [--offline]`, when built with `--features ui`, launches an Adwaita
  application window with a title/header, refresh button, and sections for
  daemon, tasks, approvals, audit, tools, and policy. Tasks render read-only
  Details buttons plus Cancel GTK buttons for cancellable states, and pending
  approvals render Details/Approve/Deny GTK buttons. When the live daemon is
  available, mutating buttons call `org.trillionnium.Agent1.CancelTask`, `Approve`,
  `ApproveScoped`, `ApproveScopedUntil`, `Deny`, `DenyScoped`, or
  `DenyScopedUntil` and rebuild the dashboard from the daemon snapshot.
  Pending approvals expose one-call, current-task, current-session,
  until-reboot, persistent, and never-allow controls both in the approval
  section action row and directly on each structured pending-approval card;
  row-level approval controls use compact labels and are split into `Decision`
  and `Remember` groups, while still sharing the same inline deny-reason and
  scoped grant TTL entries as the section controls. Approval detail dialogs and the
  Audit/Tools sections expose read-only event/manifest/tool-run Details buttons
  with schema, payload, policy, grant, run, and audit context. Audit filters now
  include task/tool-call/kind text entries plus quick kind/category preset
  buttons for common tool, approval, policy, and lifecycle event groups; kind
  filters accept comma-separated audit kind slugs across D-Bus, CLI, SQLite
  fallback, export, and GTK, so category presets can query multiple event kinds
  without widening the D-Bus ABI. Entries are prefilled from the current filter
  state after refresh/paging/presets; the GTK panel now also shows an active-view
  chip row (`all audit events`, task, tool-call, and/or kind/category) and splits
  preset buttons into `Category presets` and `Common kind presets` rows, with the
  currently active kind preset styled as suggested. Presets preserve typed/current task
  and tool-call filters and reset the cursor to the latest matching page. Active grants are listed in
  their own GTK section with Revoke buttons wired to `RevokeApprovalGrant`;
  current-task grants are persisted in SQLite and reloaded after daemon restart,
  current-session grants are live-memory-only and disappear on daemon restart,
  until-reboot grants are persisted with the Linux boot id so they survive
  daemon restart but are pruned after OS reboot, persistent grants are persisted
  until explicit revoke or expiry, and never-allow grants are negative deny-list
  entries persisted until explicit revoke or expiry.
  When the daemon is live, the GTK shell also attaches to the same D-Bus signal
  subscription path used by `trillionnium-command-center watch` and refreshes after
  task, approval, audit, and tool lifecycle events; the UI model now emits typed,
  keyed body rows with structured task, approval, grant, tool, audit-event, and
  tool-run payloads plus row-level action hints, and refreshes patch changed GTK
  sections/rows in place when possible instead of always rebuilding the full
  content box.
  `--offline` keeps the same local SQLite fallback path, does not query
  `org.trillionnium.Agent1`, and shows disabled action controls.

M3 actionability slice now exists:

- `trillionnium-command-center approve <approval-id> [--scope one_call|current_task|current_session|until_reboot|persistent]
  [--expires-in <duration>|--expires-at-unix-ms <ms>]` calls
  `org.trillionnium.Agent1.Approve`, `ApproveScoped`, or `ApproveScopedUntil` and
  reports the decided approval plus grant in text or `--json`. Current-task
  grants are persisted in the audit SQLite database, reloaded by
  `AgentService::from_store`, pruned if expired, and allow the same tool for the
  same task after daemon restart. Current-session grants are revocable
  live-memory grants for the same tool across tasks, but do not persist across
  daemon restart. Until-reboot grants persist for the same tool across tasks and
  daemon restarts, but carry the current `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` and
  are pruned on service load after an OS reboot. Persistent grants persist for
  the same tool across tasks and daemon/OS restarts until revoke or optional
  expiry.
- `trillionnium-command-center deny <approval-id> [--reason <text>] [--scope never_allow]
  [--expires-in <duration>|--expires-at-unix-ms <ms>]` calls `Deny`,
  `DenyScoped`, or `DenyScopedUntil`. Plain deny only rejects the current
  pending approval; `--scope never_allow` also creates a revocable negative
  grant for the same tool so future matching tool calls are denied by policy
  instead of asking again. The negative grant is persisted and can be TTL-bound.
- `trillionnium-command-center approval show <approval-id> [--offline] [--json]`
  renders a focused approval detail view from the live daemon snapshot or the
  read-only SQLite fallback, including approval reason/decision fields plus
  related task and tool-run context when present. The GTK shell exposes the same
  detail text through per-approval Details buttons in a modal child window;
  Details stays available offline because it does not mutate daemon state.
- `trillionnium-command-center task show <task-id> [--offline] [--json]` renders a
  focused task detail view from the live daemon snapshot or read-only SQLite
  fallback, including task metadata plus related approvals, tool runs, and
  recent audit events in the current dashboard window. The GTK shell exposes the
  same detail text through per-task Details buttons in the same modal child
  window path; Details stays available offline because it is read-only.
- `trillionnium-command-center tool show <tool-name> [--offline] [--json]` renders a
  focused tool manifest view from the live daemon snapshot or static manifest
  fallback, including full input/output schemas, executor/capability metadata,
  validation status, matching policy probe, active grants, recent tool runs, and
  related audit events. The GTK shell exposes the same detail text through
  per-tool Details buttons; Details stays available offline because it is
  read-only.
- `trillionnium-command-center tool run show <tool-call-id> [--offline] [--json]`
  renders a focused tool-run detail view from the live daemon snapshot or
  read-only SQLite fallback, including arguments, output/error, policy decision,
  related task, related approval, related manifest summary, and recent audit
  events. The GTK shell exposes the same detail text through per-run Details
  buttons for recent tool runs in the Tools section; Details stays available
  offline because it is read-only.
- `trillionnium-command-center tool run retry <tool-call-id> [--json]` calls
  `org.trillionnium.Agent1.RetryToolRun` for failed or approval-granted-awaiting-retry
  tool runs. Retry is a mutating live-daemon action, so it rejects `--offline`;
  the GTK Tools section shows Retry buttons only for retryable recent runs and
  disables them when no live daemon is available.
- `trillionnium-command-center audit list [--task <task-id>] [--tool-call <tool-call-id>]
  [--kind <kind>[,<kind>...]] [--before <audit-id>|--after <audit-id>] [--limit <n>]
  [--offline] [--json]` renders a filtered, cursor-pageable audit timeline
  without mutating daemon state. Comma-separated kind filters power GTK category
  presets such as task lifecycle, tool lifecycle, approvals, and policy while
  preserving the same read-only audit path. `audit show <audit-id>
  [--offline] [--json]` renders a focused audit event detail view with pretty
  payload plus related task, tool run, approval, and manifest context when
  present. The GTK Audit section exposes optional task/tool-call/kind filter
  entries, Older/Newer/Latest cursor paging, and read-only Details buttons for
  recent matching events; Details and paging stay available offline because they
  are read-only.
- `trillionnium-command-center audit export [--task <task-id>] [--tool-call <tool-call-id>]
  [--kind <kind>[,<kind>...]] [--before <audit-id>|--after <audit-id>] [--limit <n>]
  [--format json|jsonl|markdown|csv] [--output <path>] [--offline]` exports
  the matching audit page without mutating daemon state. JSON export includes source/filter metadata;
  JSONL is one event per line; Markdown includes a table plus payload sections;
  CSV includes stable scalar columns plus compact payload JSON.
- `trillionnium-command-center grant list [--json]` calls
  `org.trillionnium.Agent1.ListApprovalGrants` and shows active live grants. With
  `--offline`, it reads persisted local SQLite grant snapshots without making
  daemon decisions.
- `trillionnium-command-center grant revoke <grant-id> [--json]` calls
  `org.trillionnium.Agent1.RevokeApprovalGrant`, removes the grant from the live daemon
  grant store plus SQLite, and writes an `ApprovalGrantRevoked` audit event.
  Revoke still rejects `--offline` because revocation is an active daemon
  decision.
- The D-Bus JSON-string ABI parser now validates the top-level object, requires
  boolean `ok`, surfaces daemon errors, and parses typed task/approval/audit and
  action payloads with unit coverage.
- Approval actions reject `--offline` clearly because offline/local SQLite mode
  is read-only and must not fabricate daemon decisions.
- The shared UI model now carries typed task/approval detail/actions plus CLI commands
  for auditability. The current FFI shell turns enabled live-daemon actions into
  real GTK Details/Cancel/Approve-once/Approve-for-task/Approve-for-session/
  Approve-until-reboot/Approve-always/Deny/Never-allow/Revoke-grant buttons and
  refreshes the content after D-Bus decisions. Approval sections also expose an
  inline GTK deny-reason entry; Deny buttons use that custom reason when filled,
  otherwise they fall back to the default Command Center reason. The gtk-rs/
  Relm4 cleanup remains the path for richer widgets and more idiomatic widget
  state management.

Hepta embedding audit/correction slice now exists:

- `docs/HEPTA_EMBEDDING_AUDIT.md` records the inspected Dropbox Hepta workspace,
  public core contracts, `hepta_runtime::RuntimeKernel` entry points, and the
  current embedding gap.
- The audit confirms Hepta is already the native runtime/execution engine. Trillionnium OS is the supervisor/control plane for D-Bus, Command Center, approvals,
  audit, policy hooks, Phosh/session integration, and future Waydroid/mobile
  bridging.
- `trillionnium-tool-runtime` now exposes an explicit `HeptaRuntimeAdapter` boundary,
  with `LocalShimAdapter` for the current compatibility harness,
  `UnsupportedHeptaRuntimeAdapter` as a loud placeholder for the future direct
  native Hepta adapter, `RuntimeAdapterProbe` / `runtime_adapter_probe()` as a
  CLI/status-visible readiness surface, `RuntimeAdapterContract` /
  `runtime_adapter_contract()` as a CLI-visible contract draft, and
  `HeptaCatalogProbe` / `hepta_catalog_probe()` as a feature-gated read-only
  native descriptor probe.
- A direct compile-time adapter to `hepta-runtime` was not added yet because the
  audited public API exposes tool catalog/validation, policy, events, sessions,
  and demo-turn execution, but not a narrow public `invoke_tool(name,
  input_json, session, correlation)` API. Trillionnium OS should not route through a
  full demo turn or duplicate RuntimeKernel policy state just to overclaim
  embedding.

M3 task/watch/tool slice now exists:

- `trillionnium-command-center task create <title> [--description <text>]
  [--metadata-json <json>] [--json]` builds a typed `TaskInput`, validates the
  metadata JSON locally, calls `org.trillionnium.Agent1.CreateTask`, and reports the
  returned `TaskView`.
- `trillionnium-command-center task cancel <task-id> [--json]` calls
  `org.trillionnium.Agent1.CancelTask` and reports the returned cancelled `TaskView`.
- Task mutations reject `--offline` clearly for the same reason approval
  mutations do: local SQLite snapshots are read-only status material, not a
  substitute for daemon state transitions.
- `trillionnium-command-center tool list [--json] [--offline]` lists available tool
  manifests. Offline mode uses static built-in manifests.
- `trillionnium-command-center tool run <tool-name> --task <task-id>
  [--arguments-json <json>] [--json]` calls `org.trillionnium.Agent1.RunTool`. Offline
  mode rejects the mutation. `system.status` returns a successful `ToolRun` and
  output immediately; `demo.approval_echo` returns a pending approval and then
  resumes after `approve`.
- `trillionnium-command-center tool run retry <tool-call-id> [--json]` replays a
  persisted failed or approval-granted-awaiting-retry tool run through
  `org.trillionnium.Agent1.RetryToolRun`; the retry path is live-only and reuses the
  original arguments/tool-call id for auditability.
- `trillionnium-command-center watch [--json] [--limit <n>] [--once]
  [--timeout-ms <ms>]` opens a session-D-Bus signal subscription, prints an
  initial live dashboard snapshot, then streams JSON-string D-Bus signals as
  readable text or newline-delimited JSON objects. It surfaces task, approval,
  audit, and tool lifecycle signals. `--once`/`--timeout-ms` make it
  smoke-testable without leaving a long-running watcher behind.
- The GTK shell now attaches to the same D-Bus signal subscription path used by
  `watch --json` and auto-refreshes the dashboard after live events. The current
  FFI path polls the signal stream from a GLib timeout and applies section/body
  patches driven by typed `UiSection.body_rows`: unchanged cards are kept, keyed
  body rows are updated/reordered in place or inserted/removed as needed, row
  kind changes update GTK CSS classes, task, approval, grant, tool, audit-event,
  and tool-run rows render as structured header/summary/context widgets with
  nearby row-level action buttons where available, and only sections whose action
  wiring changed are rebuilt. Moving to native async GTK/glib integration remains
  part of the gtk-rs/Relm4 cleanup.

Dogfood-alpha session integration now exists under `packaging/`:

- `install-dev.sh` builds debug binaries, installs them under `~/.local/bin`,
  renders user-session templates, reloads systemd, enables, and restarts
  `trillionniumd.service`. `uninstall-dev.sh` reverses those user-session writes
  and keeps local state by default unless `--purge-state` is explicitly passed.
- `trillionnium-command-center doctor` checks the repo, installed sibling daemon
  binary, systemd user unit, session-D-Bus activation file, desktop entry,
  user-service enabled/active state, local SQLite state, live D-Bus snapshot, and
  current tool adapter. `doctor --profile desktop` extends that with passive
  Debian/GNOME readiness checks: platform/profile metadata, the Debian apt
  dependency list, GNOME UI density/adaptive spec, session hints, freedesktop
  commands, and xdg-desktop-portal user services. `doctor --profile mobile`
  extends the same model with passive Mobian/Phosh readiness checks:
  platform/profile metadata, the Mobian apt dependency list, touch-first Phosh UI
  profile metadata (Phosh/Phoc, Squeekboard, 48dp touch targets, 360dp minimum
  width, 600dp adaptive breakpoint), session hints, ModemManager,
  NetworkManager, and power visibility. `status --json` also exposes a passive
  mobile capability matrix for touch UI, shell session, modem, network, and
  power stack visibility, plus draft Mobian package/image blueprints under
  `packaging/mobian/`, draft-only device-compatibility, emulator/hardware
  smoke, rollback, aggregate mobile promotion-draft reports with blocker
  reasons from `packaging/mobian/promotion-drafts/`, and a derived
  `mobile.os_integration` blocker summary for package/image/promotion/capability
  readiness. The lightweight `trillionnium-command-center mobile
  integration-report [--summary-only|--blockers-only] [--check|--exit-code]
  [--format json|jsonl|markdown|csv] [--output <path>] [--json]` command
  renders/exports the same passive integration summary without collecting the
  full dashboard, with compact summary/blocker-only modes, an exit-code check
  mode, and JSONL/Markdown/CSV snapshot exports for scripts and heartbeat checks.
  `doctor --profile all` runs both readiness profiles as one passive
  platform matrix, which is also surfaced as structured `status --json`
  `platform_matrix` data, in text `status`, and in Command Center UI as a
  dedicated Platform readiness matrix section. `status --json` also exposes a
  passive `packaging` checklist for dogfood-alpha templates plus Debian/Mobian
  packaging scaffolds, draft-only package/image checklists, and passive
  promotion gate declarations; it intentionally reports distro package readiness
  as false until promoted package/image manifests and verification gates exist. A
  passive `verification` snapshot records Cargo/Rust tool visibility, required
  feature-gate metadata, manual gate command hints, and release blockers such as
  missing `cargo-audit` without running cargo or install scripts.
  `trillionnium-command-center selftest` then exercises the
  live control plane by creating a real task, running low-risk `system.status`,
  running medium-risk `demo.approval_echo`, approving that pending request once,
  verifying the resumed tool run, and checking matching audit evidence. On
  failures, doctor now includes focused diagnostics for systemd status, recent
  journal logs, D-Bus ping, and installed template contents.
- `platform/README.md` and `profile/README.md` document the current passive
  platform matrix.
- `platform/debian/` plus `profile/desktop-gnome/` define the first explicit
  desktop base/profile without migrating the current dev host.
- `platform/mobian/` plus `profile/mobile-phosh/` define the first mobile
  landing target without ROM/flashing work.
- `trillionnium-command-center.desktop` for Mobian/Phosh and desktop launchers.
- `trillionniumd.service` as a systemd user-unit template.
- `org.trillionnium.Agent1.service` as a session-D-Bus activation template.
- `packaging/README.md` documents install, verify, dry-run, rollback, and the
  passive packaging readiness checklist; `packaging/debian/README.md` and
  `packaging/mobian/README.md` define non-promoted distro/package scaffolds
  with draft-only package/image manifest checklists and `packaging/promotion-gates.toml`
  declares passive draft promotion path gates. Debian/GNOME and Mobian/Phosh now
  also have draft-only promotion evidence checklists under their respective
  `promotion-drafts/` directories; these are reported as draft evidence but
  deliberately do not satisfy promoted gate paths. The promotion report also
  passively validates draft evidence TOML and required draft metadata, surfacing
  valid/invalid draft counts without promoting gates; `status --json packaging`
  exposes the same all-target draft evidence count/valid/invalid summary.
  `packaging promotion-report --target all --summary-only --json` reports only
  top-level readiness/counts for lightweight automation,
  `--missing-only` reports gate gaps directly, and `--invalid-only` filters to
  malformed draft evidence for future maintenance. These support optional
  desktop/mobile filtering without running builds, installs, audits, or
  flashing.
  `status --json` also includes passive release verification metadata for local
  gate availability and command hints. This is still not a distro package.

GTK/libadwaita / gtk-rs environment note:

- Host system packages are available: `pkg-config --modversion gtk4` reports
  4.14.5 and `pkg-config --modversion libadwaita-1` reports 1.5.0.
- The production `ui` feature still uses the raw GTK/libadwaita FFI adapter while
  live actions, D-Bus refresh, and row-level controls are migrated safely.
- The gtk-rs/Relm4 migration path exists behind `--features relm4-ui`. It
  downloads/locks Relm4 0.11, launches a `SimpleComponent`, renders the existing
  `UiSection`/`UiBodyRow` dashboard model as gtk-rs widgets, migrates Details
  action hints to real gtk-rs buttons/dialogs, wires audit filter entries,
  kind presets, and Older/Newer/Latest paging through the same read-only
  `AuditTimelinePage`/local SQLite cursor path, wires the first live D-Bus
  mutating actions (Cancel task, Retry tool run, Approve/Deny approval, Revoke
  grant), attaches the same `DbusWatch` signal stream for live refresh after
  task/approval/audit/tool lifecycle events, shares Relm4 approval override
  inputs for custom deny reasons plus scoped-grant / never-allow TTLs, and folds
  dense section/card action rows behind a GTK popover-backed More menu. The FFI
  shell remains the feature-complete production path while deeper Relm4 polish is
  migrated.
- Headless GTK execution was not added in this pass; instead, the shared UI
  model has unit coverage and the UI-specific compile gates are
  `cargo check -p trillionnium-command-center --features ui` and
  `cargo check -p trillionnium-command-center --features relm4-ui`.

Known limitations after this slice:

- Tool execution is local-shim-only for built-in Trillionnium OS smoke tools. Hepta is
  the canonical native runtime; direct delegation awaits a stable public
  RuntimeKernel tool-invocation adapter. There is still no arbitrary
  process/shell executor, queue scheduler, timeout sandbox, or worker isolation
  layer in Trillionnium OS.
- Task, approval, tool, recent tool-run, and audit event screens now have first-pass read-only Details views,
  while live GTK buttons cover cancellable tasks, pending approvals, and active
  approval grants. Current approve supports one-call, durable current-task
  grants, in-memory current-session grants, boot-id-bound until-reboot grants,
  persistent grants, and never-allow negative grants; scoped grants can be
  bounded by TTL, listed, and revoked. Retry controls now cover failed and
  approval-granted-awaiting-retry tool runs. Audit list/export now cover filtered
  JSON/JSONL/Markdown/CSV snapshots plus `--before`/`--after` cursor paging;
  the GTK Audit card now exposes task/tool-call/kind filter entries, an active-view
  chip row, split category/common-kind preset rows with active preset highlighting,
  and Older/Newer/Latest page controls on top of that cursor model. Richer GTK
  widgets beyond raw FFI are still pending.
- Live D-Bus events are consumed by both the CLI watch stream and the GTK FFI
  shell. The GTK path is still intentionally minimal, but `ui_model` now exposes
  stable keyed/typed `UiBodyRow` entries with structured task, approval, grant,
  tool, audit-event, and tool-run payloads plus row-level action hints; GTK
  applies section-level plus row-level patches instead of always
  clearing/rebuilding the whole dashboard and renders those rows as structured
  cards with nearby Details/Cancel/Retry/Revoke controls where available. Richer
  approval-specific inline controls remain pending.
- Dogfood install is user-session/dev-only, not a distro package: paths are
  `~/.local/bin`, `~/.config/systemd/user`, `~/.local/share/dbus-1/services`,
  and `~/.local/share/applications`; icon assets, D-Bus activation policy, and
  privileged broker/polkit boundaries are not final.
- The current host dogfood install has been verified live with
  `trillionnium-command-center doctor`, `trillionnium-command-center doctor --profile desktop`,
  `trillionnium-command-center doctor --profile mobile`, `trillionnium-command-center doctor --profile all`,
  `trillionnium-command-center selftest`, `systemctl --user is-enabled/is-active`,
  `gdbus ... Ping`, and live
  `trillionnium-command-center status`; desktop and mobile profiles remain
  passive readiness surfaces, and the mobile profile still needs real
  Mobian/Phosh shell testing.

## v0.4 Design Alignment Note

The downloaded design document
`/home/qian-qi/下载/Trillionnium_OS_AI_Native_Design_Document_v0.4.md` has been
reviewed as a target Shell Overlay / Bridge / mobile MVP product spec, not as a
current-state implementation report. The repo-level crosswalk lives at
`../../docs/archive/2026-05-linux-mobian-concept/11-v0.4-design-alignment.md`.

Current dogfood state remains `trillionniumd` + `trillionnium-command-center`
over `org.trillionnium.Agent1`, with LocalShim as the default executor.
`trillionnium-shell` now exists only as a separate passive target-spec/report
binary, not as an interactive overlay. The future v0.4 names
`trillionnium-settings`, `ai.trillionnium.*`, fully interactive Shell Overlay
surfaces, Bridge Protocol v1 runtime ingestion, full production host package
install, OTA, flashing, and full mobile OS image claims are not implemented
facts yet. They are future gates that must be promoted with separate evidence.

The mobile integration command surface added in this slice is the current
scriptable bridge between the target v0.4 mobile story and actual dogfood state:
`trillionnium-command-center mobile integration-report` reports package/image,
promotion, and capability blockers, supports compact filters, returns readiness
exit code `2` while blocked when `--check` is used, and exports passive snapshots
as JSON/JSONL/Markdown/CSV. It does not build packages/images, run install
scripts, start services, boot emulators, probe hardware, mutate modem/network /
power/systemd state, emit D-Bus signals, write audit preview rows, register
native Hepta tools, or start/take over the sidecar.

Latest mobile packaging checkpoint: the Mobian source package path, image path,
and promoted mobile gate evidence are present as passive source artifacts, so
`mobile integration-report` exposes `source_package_path_ready=true`,
`source_image_path_ready=true`, `source_promotion_gates_ready=true`, and
`source_integration_ready=true`. The package path now also has an explicit
operator-invoked dpkg root-install smoke:
`packaging/mobian/scripts/package-install-smoke.sh` builds four `.deb` payloads,
installs them with `dpkg -i` into
`target/mobian-package-install-smoke/install-root`, verifies
`/usr/bin` binaries, Agent/Shell D-Bus services, daemon/sidecar/Shell companion
user units, packaged mobile session helpers, dpkg status/log evidence, and
emits a rootfs-style payload tarball. Evidence lives at
`docs/mobile-smoke/2026-05-15-mobian-package-install-smoke.{json,txt}` and
`packaging/mobian/promotion/package-install-smoke.toml`. Under the explicit operator-started headless
Phoc/Phosh dogfood session, the report now reaches
`mobile-os-integration-ready` with `can_package_now=true`,
`can_build_image_now=true`, and `can_integrate_now=true`; evidence is captured
in `docs/mobile-smoke/2026-05-15-mobile-package-image-integration-ready.{json,txt}`.
Outside that mobile session it remains false on this Ubuntu/GNOME dev host
because current-host Mobian/Phosh capabilities are not complete. Mobile
capability checks require a real `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` socket and visible `phosh`
process for Phosh/Wayland readiness, so sourcing the mobile dev environment
alone cannot make `can_integrate_now` true. The report keeps package/image
builds, installs, service changes, emulator boots, hardware probes, flashing,
and Android/Lineage paths disabled; only the explicit operator smoke builds
local package payloads under `target/`, and it still avoids host install,
maintainer scripts, and service enable/start.

Added `packaging/mobian/scripts/headless-mobile-session.sh start|status|stop`
as the explicit operator path for local nested Phoc/Phosh dogfood. It uses a
dedicated runtime directory, starts Phoc with the headless wlroots backend and
Phosh attached as the shell, can optionally start Waydroid when
`START_WAYDROID=1`, and cleans up its socket on stop. A source smoke verified
that `mobile integration-report --summary-only --check --json` becomes
`mobile-os-integration-ready` only while the helper-created socket and Phosh
process are alive, then returns to not-ready after stop.

## v0.4 Policy Taxonomy Crosswalk

Added a read-only `crosswalk_v04_policy_case` layer in
`trillionnium-policy-system` for the downloaded v0.4 `L0-L4`, `D0-D4`, and
`A0-A3` policy taxonomy. The crosswalk maps v0.4 target decisions into the
current dogfood vocabulary (`RiskTier`, `PolicyDecisionKind`, and
`ApprovalRequirement`) and includes regression tests for L0 allow, conservative
L1 light-confirm-to-ask, L2 explicit-confirm-to-ask, L3 strong-confirm-to-deny
until strong confirmation exists, L4 deny, Android A3 deny, D4 external/cloud
deny, untrusted-content policy recheck, privacy-mode Android notification denial,
and low-power Android launch light-confirm-to-ask.

This is compatibility evidence only: `PolicyEngine::evaluate` is unchanged, no
new runtime command is exposed, and no tool execution, sidecar behavior, D-Bus
registration, audit writes, package/image gates, or mobile readiness booleans are
changed by the crosswalk.

## v0.4 Policy Crosswalk CLI Report

Added `trillionnium-command-center policy v04-crosswalk [--json]` as a
scriptable read-only report over the v0.4 policy taxonomy crosswalk. The report
emits representative L0-L4 / D0-D4 / A0-A3 cases, their v0.4 target decisions,
and the current dogfood `RiskTier` / `PolicyDecisionKind` /
`ApprovalRequirement` mapping. It reports `policy_engine_connected=false` and
`mutates_policy=false` to make clear that it does not call or change
`PolicyEngine::evaluate`.

This is a QA/documentation surface only. It does not create approvals or grants,
run tools, mutate policy, emit D-Bus signals, write audit rows, start/take over
the sidecar, register native Hepta tools, or change mobile/package/image
readiness state.

## Bridge Protocol v1 Verifier Fixtures

Added `trillionnium-bridge-protocol` as a verifier-only foundation for the v0.4
Waydroid/Android Bridge target. The crate defines signed Bridge Protocol v1
envelopes, canonical payload bytes, HMAC-SHA256 signing/verification,
pairing/device checks, nonce freshness, duplicate event detection, monotonic
sequence checks, TTL/future-clock handling, and ack/retry/dead-letter verifier
reports. Unit tests cover canonical JSON ordering, accepted signed notification
fixtures, bad HMAC, nonce replay, stale sequence, duplicate event id, expired
TTL, future timestamp retry, wrong pairing, and aggregate fixture expectations.

Command Center now exposes a read-only QA surface:
`trillionnium-command-center bridge protocol-report [--json]`. The report emits
deterministic verifier fixtures with `verifier_only=true`,
`bridge_apk_connected=false`, `waydroid_connected=false`,
`dbus_signal_enabled=false`, `audit_write_enabled=false`, and
`tool_invoke_enabled=false`. Accepted verifier output remains policy-tainted and
is not ingested into Signal Broker.

This does not implement a Bridge APK, Android notification listener, share
receiver, package inventory, persistent bridge store, Waydroid start/stop, Android
UI automation, ADB shell, D-Bus emission, audit persistence, tool invocation, or
mobile readiness promotion.

## Bridge Replay / Pairing Store Fixtures

Added a `BridgeReplayPairingStore` trait plus an in-memory replay/pairing-store
foundation to `trillionnium-bridge-protocol`, still as verifier-only QA. The
store tracks pairing id, expected device id, HMAC secret, revoked state, last
accepted sequence, seen event ids, and seen nonces. `verify_and_record` constructs the
existing verifier context from that record, records only accepted envelopes, and
leaves retry/dead-letter outcomes out of the accepted replay cursor. Unit tests
cover accepted cursor updates, duplicate event replay, revoked pairing, unknown
pairing, and retry-without-cursor-advance.

Command Center now exposes
`trillionnium-command-center bridge replay-report [--json]`. The report runs
deterministic in-memory fixtures for accepted cursor updates, duplicate event id,
stale sequence, replayed nonce, future timestamp retry, accept-after-retry,
revoked pairing, and unknown pairing. It reports `verifier_only=true`,
`in_memory_only=true`, `persistent_storage_enabled=false`,
`bridge_apk_connected=false`, `waydroid_connected=false`,
`dbus_signal_enabled=false`, `audit_write_enabled=false`, and
`tool_invoke_enabled=false`.

This does not write SQLite, emit D-Bus signals, call tools, connect to Waydroid,
implement a Bridge APK, consume Android notifications/shares/package inventory,
or promote mobile/packaging/readiness gates. Accepted output remains
policy-tainted and local to the fixture process.

## Bridge Durable Store Plan

Added `trillionnium-command-center bridge store-plan [--json]`, a design-only
logical durable-store contract for the Bridge replay/pairing foundation. The
report defines non-writing table plans for `bridge_pairings`,
`bridge_seen_events`, `bridge_seen_nonces`, `bridge_retry_holds`, and
`bridge_dead_letters`, plus invariants for monotonic accepted sequence updates,
retry/dead-letter no-advance behavior, revocation-before-acceptance, duplicate
event/nonce rejection, redacted secret material, and policy-tainted accepted
output.

This is not SQLite and not a migration. The report sets `design_only=true`,
`persistent_storage_enabled=false`, `sqlite_enabled=false`,
`migration_writes_enabled=false`, `bridge_apk_connected=false`,
`waydroid_connected=false`, `dbus_signal_enabled=false`,
`audit_write_enabled=false`, and `tool_invoke_enabled=false`; every table plan
keeps `writes_allowed_now=false`. It does not open a database, write files, emit
D-Bus signals, persist audit rows, invoke tools, or consume Android/Waydroid
events.

## Bridge Migration Dry-Run

Added `trillionnium-command-center bridge migration-dry-run [--json]`, a
non-writing validator for the Bridge store-plan contract. It checks the source
plan status and safety flags, required logical tables, table-count and
invariant-count consistency, unique table/column names, primary key/constraint
/index column references, sensitive `secret_material_ref`, nonce-hash-only
ledger design, retry/dead-letter no-advance invariants, and policy-tainted
accepted output.

The report is still verifier/design QA only: `dry_run_only=true`,
`design_only=true`, `opens_database=false`, `database_path=null`,
`persistent_storage_enabled=false`, `sqlite_enabled=false`,
`migration_writes_enabled=false`, `bridge_apk_connected=false`,
`waydroid_connected=false`, `dbus_signal_enabled=false`,

## Bridge Schema Preview

Added `trillionnium-command-center bridge schema-preview [--json]`, a
non-executing schema/DDL preview generated from the Bridge durable store plan.
It renders deterministic SQLite-like `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` and
`CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` statements for the logical pairings, seen-events,
seen-nonces, retry-holds, and dead-letters tables, plus per-statement SHA-256
digests and a whole-schema hash for review/diff stability.

The report remains review-only: `preview_only=true`, `design_only=true`,
`opens_database=false`, `database_path=null`, `persistent_storage_enabled=false`,
`sqlite_enabled=false`, `ddl_execution_enabled=false`,
`migration_writes_enabled=false`, `bridge_apk_connected=false`,
`waydroid_connected=false`, `dbus_signal_enabled=false`,
`audit_write_enabled=false`, and `tool_invoke_enabled=false`; every statement
keeps `executes_now=false`. No database is opened, no DDL is executed, no files
are written, and no Android/Waydroid/D-Bus/audit/tool side effect occurs.

## Bridge Throwaway Store Smoke

Added `trillionnium-command-center bridge throwaway-store-smoke [--json]`, a
verifier-only SQLite execution smoke for the Bridge schema. It opens only a
`rusqlite::Connection::open_in_memory()` backend, executes the generated schema
preview statements there, checks planned table/index presence, and probes core
constraints: active pairing insertion, invalid pairing-state rejection, duplicate
device rejection, accepted event insertion, duplicate event rejection, raw nonce
shape rejection, retry holds not advancing the accepted cursor, and dead letters
not being promoted to accepted events.

The report intentionally distinguishes throwaway DDL execution from persistent
storage promotion: `throwaway_only=true`, `in_memory_database=true`,
`database_path=null`, `persistent_storage_enabled=false`,
`migration_writes_enabled=false`, `bridge_apk_connected=false`,
`waydroid_connected=false`, `android_ingestion_enabled=false`,
`dbus_signal_enabled=false`, `audit_write_enabled=false`, and
`tool_invoke_enabled=false`. It reports `sqlite_enabled=true` and
`ddl_execution_enabled=true` only for the ephemeral in-memory verifier backend;
no database path, migration file, Android/Waydroid endpoint, D-Bus signal, audit
row, or tool invocation is touched.

Text output, JSON output, CLI parsing, unit tests, and the Bridge UI command
hints now expose this smoke as a developer gate before any future persistent
Bridge replay store or Android ingestion promotion. It is not folded into
`status`, `bridge readiness-report`, or `bridge evidence-report`, so those
passive aggregates still do not open SQLite or execute DDL while remaining
script-friendly.

## Bridge SQLite Replay Store Smoke

Added `trillionnium-command-center bridge sqlite-replay-smoke [--json]`, a
second verifier-only in-memory SQLite gate that runs signed Bridge envelope
fixtures through a throwaway SQLite replay-store path. Unlike
`throwaway-store-smoke`, which manually probes schema constraints, this smoke
uses verifier outcomes to write accepted-event, nonce, retry-hold, and
dead-letter rows. It checks accepted cursor advancement, duplicate event
rejection, stale sequence rejection, hashed nonce replay rejection, retry without
accepted-cursor advance, acceptance after retry, revoked pairing dead-lettering,
and unknown pairing dead-lettering.

The report currently passes `fixture_count=8`, `passed_fixture_count=8`,

pairing ends with `last_accepted_sequence=2`, `seen_event_id_count=2`, and
`seen_nonce_count=2`; the retry fixture snapshot shows the cursor still at `1`,
proving retry rows remain isolated from accepted replay state.

Safety remains explicit: `throwaway_only=true`, `in_memory_database=true`,
`database_path=null`, `persistent_storage_enabled=false`,
`migration_writes_enabled=false`, `bridge_apk_connected=false`,
`waydroid_connected=false`, `android_ingestion_enabled=false`,
`dbus_signal_enabled=false`, `audit_write_enabled=false`, and

## Arm64 Mobian Fogos Destructive Install Execution Receipt Smoke

Promoted the arm64 Mobian fogos destructive install execution receipt smoke. It
imports the already-recorded authorized fastboot install log and post-reboot
observation log from
`target/mobian-arm64-fogos-destructive-install-20260518T092406Z/`; the
importer itself is read-only and does not run ADB, fastboot, flash, wipe,
repartition, sideload, reboot, relock, install, or release push.

The authorized install run wrote `boot_a`, `boot_b`, `vendor_boot_a`,
`vendor_boot_b`, `dtbo_a`, `dtbo_b`, `vbmeta_a`, and `vbmeta_b`.
The original locally generated `vbmeta_system_a` image failed bootloader
preflash validation because its rollback-index location did not match the
accepted fogos child-vbmeta header shape. A corrected verification-disabled
`vbmeta_system.img` with rollback index 28 and header rollback-index location
0 was generated and accepted; `vbmeta_a`, `vbmeta_b`, and
`vbmeta_system_b` were then written from the corrected image. The sparse
`super.img` was flashed, the first reboot fell back to fastboot because both
slots were marked unbootable/retry=0, slot `b` was reactivated, and a second
reboot was executed. That slot also exhausted retries and returned to fastboot,
so a candidate2 boot image was generated with the Mobian initramfs carried as
the `boot.img` ramdisk, flashed to `boot_a` and `boot_b`, slot `b` was
reactivated, and another reboot was executed. The candidate2 post-reboot host
observation window saw no fastboot device, no ADB device, no target USB gadget,
and no USB network identity.

## Arm64 Mobian Fogos Userdata Rootfs Candidate Execution Receipt Smoke

Promoted the arm64 Mobian fogos userdata-rootfs candidate execution receipt
smoke. It imports already-recorded candidate3/candidate4 execution logs; the
importer itself is read-only and does not run ADB, fastboot, flash, wipe,
repartition, sideload, reboot, relock, rollback, install, or release push.

The receipt records the follow-up after the destructive install attempt returned
to bootloader fastboot. A candidate3 boot image was built with the fogos kernel,
the Mobian initramfs as the boot ramdisk, and kernel cmdline
`root=/dev/block/by-name/userdata rootwait rw rootfstype=ext4`; candidate3 also
included an empty vendor_boot ramdisk image while preserving the fogos DTB and
vendor cmdline. Bootloader fastboot denied direct `userdata` flashing, so the
run temporarily restored original fogos `boot.img` and `vendor_boot.img`, booted
userspace fastbootd, flashed the sparse Mobian rootfs image to `userdata`,
reflashed candidate3 boot/vendor_boot, reactivated slot `b`, and rebooted.
Candidate3 later returned to bootloader fastboot. Candidate4 then kept the same
userdata-rootfs boot image but restored the original fogos `vendor_boot.img` on
both slots, reactivated slot `b`, and rebooted. Candidate4's observation window
initially saw no fastboot, no ADB, no target USB identity, and no USB network
interface; the later host check showed the device returned to bootloader
fastboot, with both slots marked unbootable and retry count zero.

## Arm64 Mobian Fogos Candidate5 Handoff Execution Receipt Smoke

Promoted the arm64 Mobian fogos candidate5 handoff execution receipt smoke. It
imports already-recorded candidate5 execution and observation logs; the importer
itself is read-only and does not run ADB, fastboot, flash, wipe, repartition,
sideload, reboot, relock, rollback, install, or release push.

Candidate5 replaced the previous print-and-poweroff initramfs with a handoff
initramfs that scans `/sys/class/block/*/uevent` for `PARTNAME=userdata`,
falls back to `blkid` matching `LABEL="trillionniumfs"` or UUID
`979d4f6b-40f7-400a-b726-5763cb12c2a8`, mounts that ext4 rootfs at
`/newroot`, writes a target-local handoff marker when possible, moves
`/dev`/`/proc`/`/sys`, and executes `switch_root /newroot /sbin/init`.
The run flashed candidate5 `boot.img` and `vendor_boot.img` to both A/B
slots, set slot `b` active, verified slot `b` was bootable with retry count
7, and rebooted. The 8-minute observation window plus late host check saw no
fastboot, no ADB, no Motorola/Android/Qualcomm target USB identity, and no USB
network interface.

## Arm64 Mobian Fogos Candidate6 USB Gadget Diagnostic Receipt Smoke

Promoted the arm64 Mobian fogos candidate6 USB gadget diagnostic receipt smoke.
The importer is read-only: it consumes already-recorded candidate6 fastboot,
observation, current-host, and serial-read logs and does not run ADB/Fastboot,
flash, wipe, repartition, sideload, reboot, relock, rollback, install, or
release push.

Candidate6 intentionally stops at the initramfs boundary instead of switching
root. It configures a configfs USB ACM gadget as `18d1:4ee7`, then stays in a
diagnostic loop. The real run flashed candidate6 `boot.img` and
`vendor_boot.img` to both A/B slots, set slot `b` active, verified retry count
7, and rebooted. Host observation proved `18d1:4ee7`, udev model
`Fogos_Candidate6_USB_Diagnostic`, serial `ZY32JLVHGN-candidate6`, driver
`cdc_acm`, and `/dev/ttyACM0`. Fastboot/ADB/USB-network stayed absent, and
sudo serial read produced no shell output because candidate6 did not start an
interactive shell. Candidate7 USB shell diagnostic artifacts are prepared for
the next manual fastboot intake.

## Arm64 Mobian Fogos Candidate14/15 Regression Forensics Smoke

Promoted the arm64 Mobian fogos candidate14/15 regression forensics smoke. It
consumes the candidate10-13, candidate14, candidate15, and
candidate9-restore-after-candidate15 receipts plus target-local
initramfs/vendor_boot artifacts. The gate confirms candidate9 recovered after
candidate15, then narrows the no-transport regression cluster before any new
flash: `boot.img` is identical across candidate9/13/14/15, DTB hashes are
identical, vendor_boot container sizes are identical, candidate15 preserves the
candidate9 non-init payload/file list and USB identity, and candidate13 is
smaller than candidate9 but still regressed. The strongest common cluster is
therefore the selected PARTNAME uevent status/probe path in early init; the
failing status path invokes `grep '^PARTNAME='` while `/bin/grep` is not
materialized in the initramfs. Root cause remains unproven because no serial or
kmsg capture exists from the failing candidate13/14/15 boots.

## Field Frame P0 Late-Chain Source-Binding Full Suite Closure - 2026-07-05

future-plan and acceptance-path semantics guards verify an explicit
source-binding graph instead of trusting singleton report names alone. The new
checks require each configured source report to be the only matching entry in
the suite report index, require the downstream report's evidence path to point
at that exact indexed source, and require the downstream evidence SHA field to
match the source report's computed SHA-256.

## Field Frame P0 No-Device Suite Report Isolation Fix

Date: 2026-06-14

While validating the raw-key product boundary, the full no-device suite exposed
a stale-report coupling in the controlled real UI mount guard chain. The
rollback dry-run receipt, runtime dry-run, attempt authorization ledger, and
authorization request packet guards used `latest_report` from `target/` even
when the no-device suite had already generated fresher upstream reports in the
same `OUT_DIR`. After `main.rs` changed, this caused artifact hash mismatches
against older report directories rather than a product regression.

Fixed the guard chain to prefer same-`OUT_DIR` upstream reports first, and fall
back to `latest_report` only when the local suite artifact is absent.

Validated chain after the fix:

- rollback dry-run receipt: `14/14`, artifact hashes `4/4`
- runtime dry-run: `18/18`
- attempt authorization ledger: `16/16`
- authorization request packet: `16/16`

The full no-device suite then passed at
`target/resident-no-device-guard-suite-after-raw-key-product-acceptance-fixed2/`
with `status=pass-public-release-blocked`, `public_release_ready=false`,
`resident_secret_like_matches=0`, `resident_dangerous_command_matches=0`, and
`resident_report_manifest_integrity_failures=0`.

intent text contract extension. The chain confirms the remaining native path

  passed `38/38`; `exclusive` mode preserves pointer delivery and produces

  and

Added the native input-method protocol driver harness spike:
`resident-field-frame-p0-controlled-real-ui-mount-real-surface-native-input-method-protocol-driver-harness-spike-guard-smoke.sh`.

`zwp_input_method_v2` driver before the Shell service-backed text-input probe,
and tests whether a delayed protocol-level `commit_string` can be returned to
Shell.

`deactivate` is not a valid native return path; the next hardening target is
the missing `input_method.activate` source, not merely adding a service driver

initramfs path but was not copied into the switchrooted Mobian rootfs, so the
target reached Phosh without starting the bridge.

now copies `/usr/local/sbin/trillionnium-fogos-touch-uinput-bridge` into
`/newroot/usr/local/sbin/trillionnium-fogos-touch-uinput-bridge` before
